quick.summary: Break massive queries into readable blocks.
quick.takeaway: Write queries top to bottom in clear steps.

beats.line: My query has brackets inside brackets inside brackets. How do I fix a mistake?
Imagine reading a book where chapter two is stuffed inside chapter one.
Exactly. If the middle part breaks, the whole thing crashes.
Pull them apart. Write one idea at a time, from top to bottom.

board.text: Write one idea at a time

beats.line: We call this a common table expression.
Can I just say step by step blocks?
Yes. Step by step blocks are much easier to read and test.
So I name the first part, then reference it in the second part.
Now anyone can read your code like a very clear story.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of breaking a large query into smaller blocks?
options: It is easier to read, test, and find mistakes.
It automatically makes the database run faster.
It allows you to bypass security permissions.
It takes less code to write overall.
quiz.explanation: Separating ideas makes the logic transparent so anyone can follow the steps and test them.

quiz.question: Nesting queries deeply inside each other is the recommended way to write complex logic.
quiz.explanation: Nesting makes it very hard to see where things break. Pulling them out into steps is much safer.
